overview: Two subsets of CD4+ helper T cells that polarize the immune response toward different threats — intracellular pathogens versus parasites/allergens.
genZNote: Th1 calls in the special forces for intracellular invaders. Th2 calls in backup for parasites and allergy drama.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A CD4+ T-helper subset that drives cell-mediated immunity against intracellular pathogens by activating macrophages and cytotoxic responses.
aspects.valueB: A CD4+ T-helper subset that drives humoral immunity and responses against parasites, and is central to allergic reactions.

aspects.label: Primary Target
aspects.valueA: Intracellular pathogens — viruses, intracellular bacteria (e.g. Mycobacterium tuberculosis).

aspects.label: Effector Mechanism
aspects.valueA: Activates macrophages and promotes cytotoxic T-cell responses.
aspects.valueB: Promotes B-cell class switching to IgE and recruits eosinophils and mast cells.

aspects.label: Associated Conditions
aspects.valueA: Implicated in some autoimmune diseases (e.g. multiple sclerosis) via excessive activation.
aspects.valueB: Implicated in allergic disease, asthma, and atopic conditions via excessive activation.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: IFN-gamma driven, activates macrophages for intracellular threats.
aspects.valueB: IL-4/IL-5/IL-13 driven, drives IgE and eosinophil responses.
